# Decision log — constant-checking

## [#1] 2026-09-30 · DISCOVERY · 5 Research Setting
Our sample comes mostly from the authors' own networks, plus Mechanical Turk. Theoretical sampling never aimed at a representative population — so how far does the theory actually travel beyond the people we reached, and should "What does it change?" and "Where does it stop?" say so? [tentative, src: gerlach-cenfetelli-2020 p. 1709; 1721]

## [#2] 2026-09-30 · DISCOVERY · 9 Boundary Conditions and Limitations
We argue the theory's cultural and legal boundary mostly through where our sample lives — Europe and the United States — and a passing note on how checking is classified elsewhere. Should "Where does it stop?" say plainly that our causal account assumes a society with comparably open, unrestricted access to IT? [tentative, src: gerlach-cenfetelli-2020 p. 1707; 1721-1722]

## [#3] 2026-09-30 · DISCOVERY · 4 Theoretical Constructs and Relationships
"What is it made of?" rests on telling habitual checking apart from the deliberate instances we set aside in "What did we find?". But "How do we look?" never says how we actually drew that line beyond our own coding judgment and how participants labeled themselves in hindsight. Can we name a criterion, or admit the boundary is asserted rather than measured? [tentative, src: gerlach-cenfetelli-2020 p. 1712-1713]

## [#4] 2026-09-30 · DISCOVERY · 6 Research Design and Analysis
Our answer to the self-report worry — that participants were "generally very self-critical" — comes from the same interviews and surveys the worry is about. Is there anything outside that data that tells us people were not still under-reporting? [tentative, src: gerlach-cenfetelli-2020 p. 1721]

## [#5] 2026-09-30 · DISCOVERY · 3 Research Question
"What exactly do we ask?" asks when checking leads to positive or negative outcomes, but "What did we find?" answers in a different vocabulary — intended versus unintended — and says outright that it avoids labeling outcomes that way. Should the question and the finding speak the same language? [tentative, src: gerlach-cenfetelli-2020 p. 1706; 1717]
